How to use the Image Compressor & Converter

  1. Drop one or more images onto the box, or click it to pick files.
  2. Choose an output format. WebP usually gives the smallest files; PNG keeps every pixel.
  3. Adjust quality and an optional max width to resize large photos.
  4. Download each image, or grab them all at once.

Frequently asked questions

Are my images uploaded to a server?

No. Compression runs entirely in your browser using the HTML canvas API. Your files never leave your device, which also makes it fast.

Which format should I choose?

WebP is supported by all modern browsers and is typically 25–35% smaller than JPG at the same visual quality. Use JPG for maximum compatibility and PNG when you need lossless quality or transparency without artifacts.

What quality setting is best?

For photos on the web, 70–80% is a great balance; most people cannot see a difference from the original, while file sizes drop dramatically.

Is there a file size or count limit?

There is no artificial limit. Very large images depend on your device memory, but typical photos of 5–20 MB work fine.
